text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for testing the citation checker.

passages.source_passage: Board update, March 2024: The Kelewa Water Trust completed 14 new boreholes across Namboro District between July and December 2023, bringing the total under the programme to 38. Household latrine coverage in the six target villages rose from 41% to 67%, largely through the sanitation marketing pilot led by local masons. However, the borehole at Tindiri did not pass its first water quality test and has been closed until a replacement filter arrives. Community water committees collected user fees at eleven of the fourteen new sites. We have not yet recruited the second hygiene promoter approved by the board in January, and the vacancy is delaying handwashing sessions in two schools. Management recommends extending the recruitment window by six weeks.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation of the Little Steps Playgroup Network in Oruvale Province covered the period from April 2022 to September 2023. Evaluators visited 22 of the network's 35 playgroups and interviewed 140 caregivers. Average weekly attendance reached 18 children per group, against a target of 15. Caregivers reported that reading aloud at home had become more common, with 58% saying they now shared picture books at least three times a week. The evaluation did not find consistent use of the developmental screening tool, and facilitators in rural groups had never received refresher training. Volunteer turnover was high, with roughly one in four facilitators leaving within their first year. The team recommends a shorter screening form and a quarterly mentoring visit for every group.

passages.source_passage: In the 2023 school year, the Sahel Lunchbox Initiative served daily hot meals in 46 primary schools across the Kanfara region, reaching 12,400 pupils. Thanks to your grant, we sourced 62% of grains and pulses from local smallholder cooperatives, up from 40% the previous year. Enrolment in participating schools rose by nine percent, and average attendance on market days improved noticeably. Supply wasn't steady throughout the year: fuel shortages in February meant that four schools could not cook for eleven days. We did not meet the target of fortifying all rice with micronutrients, as the regional mill was closed for repairs. Parent committees contributed firewood and labour in every school, an in-kind value we estimate at 18,000 dollars.

passages.source_passage: Board update for the quarter ending 30 June 2024. The Marisol Coast Preparedness Programme now operates 27 siren towers along the Bayana shoreline, and 9 of them were upgraded to solar power this quarter. During the May storm surge drill, 81% of registered households reached an evacuation point within twenty minutes. No fatalities were recorded when Cyclone Pera made landfall in April, although two fishing boats were lost. Our SMS alert system didn't reach households in the northern islands because the mobile mast at Corran was damaged. Village volunteers relayed warnings by megaphone instead. The board is asked to approve 35,000 dollars for a backup radio network before the next cyclone season begins in November.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 academic year, the Puente Becas Fund supported 210 girls in lower and upper secondary schools across the highland municipalities of San Ilario and Cuchumal. Scholarships covered tuition, uniforms, and bus fares, and 94% of recipients completed the year. Thirty-one scholars sat the national bachillerato exam, and twenty-six passed, compared with a regional pass rate for girls of 52%. We were not able to open the planned dormitory in Cuchumal, because the municipal land transfer was never finalised. Mentors reported that early marriage remained the main reason for dropout, accounting for seven of the twelve girls who left. In 2024 we will add a parent dialogue series in partnership with local health promoters.

passages.source_passage: Board update, October 2023. The Haven Bridge protection team in Dalmeen Camp now holds 1,180 open case files, an increase of 15% since June. Caseworkers completed best-interest assessments for 64 unaccompanied children and referred 23 survivors of gender-based violence to the clinic run by our partner. The new confidential interview room opened in August, and staff report that women are more willing to disclose concerns there. However, we haven't been able to reduce the average waiting time for a first appointment, which is still nine days. Two caseworker posts were not renewed after donor funding ended in September. We propose redeploying one community outreach worker to intake duties and introducing a phone triage line staffed three mornings a week.

passages.source_passage: Board update for the second half of 2023. Our Ubuntu Home Care volunteers in the Mavuso and Lerato wards made 3,450 home visits to 512 clients living with HIV. Viral load suppression among clients with a recent test stood at 88%, up from 79% a year earlier. Volunteers delivered medication refills to bedridden clients and screened 140 household members for tuberculosis. No volunteer stipends were paid late during this period, which was not the case in early 2023. Retention remains a concern, as six of our 48 volunteers resigned, citing transport costs. The new motorbike for the supervisor arrived in November but wasn't registered until mid-December. We ask the board to note that the waiting list for home-based care now stands at seventy households.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring report, Quarter 3, 2024. The Kinship Path service in Rovena District placed 19 children with approved foster families between July and September, bringing the number of children in active placements to 74. Family tracing teams located relatives for 11 separated children, and eight of those children were reunified after home assessments. Three reunifications were postponed because the receiving households did not yet meet minimum safety standards. All foster carers received a monitoring visit within 30 days of placement, meeting the quarterly target. No child was moved between more than two placements during the period. However, case notes were not uploaded to the database for 12% of visits, mainly in the remote eastern sub-counties where connectivity is poor.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, with support from the Tanaro Health Foundation, the NetSafe Campaign distributed 86,000 long-lasting insecticidal nets across four districts of Lumbaza Province. Registration teams enumerated 41,200 households, and 92% of them collected their nets at a distribution point within the planned two-week window. A follow-up survey in November found that 71% of children under five had slept under a net the previous night. Hang-up visits were not completed in Kesula district, because heavy rains washed out the access roads for most of October. We never received the final consignment of 5,000 nets from the port, so pregnant women attending antenatal clinics were prioritised for the remaining stock. Malaria cases at sentinel health centres fell by a third compared with 2022.

passages.source_passage: Background. Since the 2021 floods, demand for psychosocial support in the Ardwen Valley has grown sharply, yet the district has only two psychiatric nurses for a population of about 180,000. The Clearwater Listening Circles project has trained 36 lay counsellors, who held 2,900 individual and group sessions between January 2022 and June 2024. An internal review found that 63% of clients reported lower distress scores after six sessions. Many people still do not seek help, because stigma around mental illness remains strong and services are not available in the two upland parishes. Lay counsellors have never had access to regular clinical supervision. This proposal requests funding to expand the model to the upland parishes and to contract a part-time clinical psychologist.
